Read each of these CUSTOMER dashboard page files IN FULL and analyze them:
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx  (952 lines — the big one, read all)
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx
- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/games/page.tsx

- /opt/nxeon/app/dashboard/order/page.tsx  (7 lines — likely a redirect stub)

For EACH route report, in terse bullet form:
- Coherent/current? (yes/partial/no)
- Dead / stale / redundant UI (be specific — placeholder text, "coming soon", disabled buttons, TODO, hardcoded/mock data, commented-out blocks, features gated off)
- UX gaps (missing states: empty/loading/error, no confirmation, no back-link, dead-end flows)
- Half-finished / orphaned pieces
- Concrete improvement, each tagged P1 (broken/misleading/blocks money or core flow), P2 (notable gap/inconsistency), or P3 (polish)

Cite exact file paths and line numbers or code snippets for load-bearing findings. Be specific, not generic. Do NOT write any report file — return your findings directly as your final message in structured markdown grouped by route.

content.text:
I have everything needed. Here are my findings.

# Nxeon customer dashboard — page-by-page audit

Scope note: these are Next.js server components that fetch data and delegate rendering to client components. Findings below focus on the page files themselves; where a load-bearing conclusion depends on a referenced component or lib, I checked it.

---

## `/dashboard/deploy` — `app/dashboard/deploy/page.tsx`
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. This is the unified "Deploy hub" and single source of truth for all order/checkout wizards (VPS, hosting, game, email). Well-commented, money-path gating is careful.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:**
  - `GAME_META` map (lines 32–39) is duplicated verbatim in `app/dashboard/games/page.tsx` (lines 11–18). Two copies of the same game name/glyph table — DRY hazard; a game added in one place silently gets a `🎮` fallback in the other. **P3**
  - Email order flow is wired in here (lines 198–240) but there is **no "Mailboxes"/email product entry in the Compute nav** — email lives under the "Mail" section (`Mailboxes` → `/dashboard/email`). So the deploy hub carries a fifth product (`email`) whose discoverability depends entirely on `?product=` deep-links or DeployHub's internal tabs. Confirm DeployHub surfaces it. **P2**
- **UX gaps:** Loading state is handled (Suspense fallback, line 251). Empty/degraded states are handled by passing `vps: null` / `game: null` when no plans exist (lines 80–82, 186–188) — DeployHub must render a graceful "product unavailable" for those nulls; worth verifying it doesn't render a blank tab. **P2**
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** None. This is the most current page in the set.
- **Improvement:** Extract `GAME_META` to a shared module (e.g. `lib/games`) and import in both `deploy` and `games` pages. **P3**

---

## `/dashboard/servers` — `app/dashboard/servers/page.tsx`
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Clean list-or-empty pattern.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** None.
- **UX gaps:** No explicit error state — if `db.server.findMany` throws it bubbles to the route error boundary (acceptable). Empty state (lines 46–53) and loading via `AutoRefresh` for transitional servers (line 41) are both present. Good.
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** `endpoint` uses `process.env.PUBLIC_IP` (line 35); if unset in an env, endpoint silently becomes `undefined:port`. Minor. **P3**
- **Improvement:** None material.

---

## `/dashboard/servers/[id]` — `app/dashboard/servers/[id]/page.tsx` (the 952-line detail page)
- **Coherent/current?** Yes — extensively so. This is the workhorse. Every money-figure (renewal badge, RenewalCard, cancel refund, resize, backup upsell) is routed through shared quote functions (`renewalQuote`, `backupUpgradeQuote`, `terminationRefundCents`) so displayed === charged. Comments cite prior incidents (game-plan mispricing, tax-inclusivity, backup-health honesty). Genuinely well-maintained.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:**
  - No literal dead code, TODOs, or "coming soon". States are gated on real status/PVE availability.
- **UX gaps (mostly handled well):**
  - PVE-unavailable degradation is explicit for live stats (line 320), snapshots (465), backups (582) — good.
  - **Tab deep-link trust:** `searchParams.tab` is passed raw to `ServerTabs` as `initialTab` (line 937). If a game-only tab (`manage`) is requested via `?tab=manage` on a non-game server, `manage` is `undefined` (line 939) — verify `ServerTabs` falls back to Overview rather than showing an empty pane. **P2**
  - **Backup restore claim vs. reality:** empty-backups copy says "restores are handled by support within minutes" (line 587) yet a `BackupRestore` self-service component is rendered right below (line 612). Mixed messaging — is restore self-service or support-gated? Reconcile the copy. **P2**
  - No back-link to `/dashboard/servers` in the header (the hosting detail page *does* have "← All hosting", line 39 of that file). Inconsistent; a customer deep on a server page has only browser-back. **P3**
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** None. `ControlPanel` (cPanel-style, line 940) is always rendered as a tab even for plain VPS — confirm it degrades sensibly on a non-hosting VM rather than showing empty cPanel chrome. **P2**
- **Improvement:** Add an "← All servers" link in the header block (lines 880–905) for parity with the hosting detail page. **P3**

---

## `/dashboard/hosting` — `app/dashboard/hosting/page.tsx`
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Correctly reduced to a manage-only view; checkout moved to the deploy hub (comment lines 9–12).
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** None.
- **UX gaps:** No empty state in the page itself — delegated to `HostingClient` (line 21). Verify `HostingClient` renders an empty state when `accounts` is `[]` (the page has no fallback of its own, unlike servers/games which handle empty inline). **P2**
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** None.
- **Improvement:** For consistency with `servers`/`games`, consider handling the empty-accounts case at the page level or confirm HostingClient does. **P3**

---

## `/dashboard/hosting/[id]` — `app/dashboard/hosting/[id]/page.tsx`
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Clean: owner-or-admin enforced in `getHostingAccount`, `notFound()` on throw/null (lines 19–24).
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** None.
- **UX gaps:** Good — has back-link ("← All hosting", line 39), transitional banner (43–47), HTTPS/status badges. This is the model the servers detail page should copy for the back-link.
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** None.
- **Improvement:** None material.

---

## `/dashboard/games` — `app/dashboard/games/page.tsx`
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Manage-only list; deploy moved to hub.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:**
  - Duplicate `GAME_META` (lines 11–18) — see deploy finding. **P3**
  - Cards link to `/dashboard/servers/${s.id}` (line 63), **not** a `games/[id]` route (confirmed no such route exists — only `page.tsx` in the dir). Intentional and consistent (game servers reuse the server detail page), but the "Manage →" affordance jumps a customer out of the Games section into Servers with no visual continuity. Minor UX seam. **P3**
- **UX gaps:** Empty state (47–54) and `AutoRefresh` for transitional (38) present. Good.
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** None.
- **Improvement:** Share `GAME_META`. **P3**

---

## `/dashboard/volumes` — `app/dashboard/volumes/page.tsx`
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. Simple, correct.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** None.
- **UX gaps:** No page-level empty state — delegated to `Volumes` component (line 51). Server-options list is filtered to `status: "RUNNING"` (line 21), so a customer whose only server is STOPPED sees "no servers to attach to" with no explanation that stopping is the cause. Worth a hint in the `Volumes` component. **P3**
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** None.
- **Improvement:** None material.

---

## `/dashboard/nxcloud` — `app/dashboard/nxcloud/page.tsx` (ORPHANED — confirmed)
- **Coherent/current?** Partial. The page is fully built and renders, but it is **unreachable from the customer nav.** Confirmed: `app/dashboard/layout.tsx` nav array (lines 28–88) has **no `/dashboard/nxcloud` entry**, and it is **not** in the `FEATURE_HREF` gate map (lines 14–26) either — so unlike `sites`/`calendar` it isn't "hidden by a flag," it was simply never added to nav. Only reachable by typing the URL. **P2** (dead surface / orphaned route)
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:**
  - Ordering is gated OFF by default: `getSettingBool("nxcloud_ordering_enabled", false)` (line 18), enforced server-side in `lib/actions-nxcloud.ts:82`. So even if a user reaches the page, the order path refuses. The page renders a full plan/pricing grid (`NxcloudClient`, lines 21–37) that leads to a dead "order" button whenever ordering is disabled — verify `NxcloudClient` visibly disables/hides purchase CTAs when `orderingEnabled=false` rather than letting a click hit the server-side refusal. **P2**
- **UX gaps:** No indication to the user that this is a preview/unlaunched product. Because it's off-nav and order-disabled, it's effectively a hidden staging surface shipped to prod.
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** The whole route. Also note `ServersPage` deliberately hides nxcloud-backed servers from the VPS list (`nxcloudInstance: { is: null }`, servers/page.tsx line 17) — so nxcloud instances have **no** reachable management surface once nav omits nxcloud. If a customer ever provisioned one, they'd have nowhere in-nav to manage it. **P1** (if any nxcloud instances can exist, they're unmanageable from nav)
- **Improvement:** Either (a) add nxcloud to nav behind a proper `feature_nxcloud` flag in `FEATURE_HREF` so it's consistent with sites/calendar gating, or (b) if it's not launching, move the route out of the prod dashboard tree. Right now it's neither shipped nor cleanly hidden. **P2**

---

## `/dashboard/sites` — `app/dashboard/sites/page.tsx` (website builder — flag OFF by default)
- **Coherent/current?** Partial. Code is complete and current, but the feature is gated off: `feature_website_builder` defaults `false` (layout.tsx line 127), so the nav entry (line 53) is hidden by default.
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI / gating hazard:**
  - **The route itself is NOT server-side gated.** `sites/page.tsx` and `sites/[id]/page.tsx` never check `feature_website_builder`. The layout comment (lines 21–23) explicitly says the flag "only gates the nav entry… the routes/code stay intact." So any logged-in user who knows/guesses `/dashboard/sites` reaches a fully-working, un-flagged website builder even while the feature is officially "off." For servers/games/hosting the comment claims order actions are refused server-side; for sites the create/publish actions in `lib/actions-sites.ts` have **no feature-flag check** (`publishSite`, lines 254–279, enqueues a real `SITE_PUBLISH` job unconditionally). A customer can create and publish sites through a feature that's supposed to be dark. **P1** (unlaunched feature is reachable + fully functional via direct URL)
  - **Stale comment:** layout.tsx line 22 says the publish path "is dormant (`ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH`)". Grep finds **no `ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH` anywhere in the codebase** — and `publishSite` enqueues a real job with no such guard. The comment describes a safety that doesn't exist. **P2**
- **UX gaps:** `AutoRefresh` while publishing (line 44) is handled. Empty state delegated to `SitesManager`.
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** The feature is in the "shipped-but-hidden" limbo — code live in prod, nav hidden, no route/action gate.
- **Improvement:** Add a server-side `feature_website_builder` guard at the top of both sites pages (and in `createSite`/`publishSite`) that `notFound()`s or refuses when the flag is off, matching the "server-side refusals" the other products rely on. Remove or correct the `ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH` comment. **P1**

---

## `/dashboard/sites/[id]` — `app/dashboard/sites/[id]/page.tsx` (site editor)
- **Coherent/current?** Partial (same flag limbo as the list page).
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** None internally.
- **UX gaps:**
  - Ownership enforced (`site.userId !== user.id → notFound`, line 18) — good.
  - Same missing feature-flag guard as the list page — directly reachable while feature is dark. **P1** (rolled into the sites P1 above)
  - `document` can be `null` if the draft is missing or fails `isSiteDocument` validation (lines 24–25); it's passed straight to `SiteEditor` (line 38). Verify `SiteEditor` renders a recoverable state for a null document rather than a blank/crashing editor. **P2**
- **Half-finished/orphaned:** Part of the dark website-builder feature.
- **Improvement:** Gate server-side; ensure `SiteEditor` handles `document === null`. **P2**

---

## `/dashboard/order` — `app/dashboard/order/page.tsx`
- **Coherent/current?** Yes. 7-line redirect stub → `/dashboard/deploy` (as expected).
- **Dead/stale/redundant UI:** None, though `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (line 3) on a pure static redirect is unnecessary. **P3**
- **UX gaps:** None (server redirect).
- **Improvement:** Cosmetic only — could drop `force-dynamic`. **P3**

---

## Cross-cutting summary
- **P1 (broken/misleading/blocks core-flow):**
  1. **Website builder reachable & fully functional via direct URL despite being flag-off** — no server-side route/action guard in `sites/page.tsx`, `sites/[id]/page.tsx`, or `publishSite` (`lib/actions-sites.ts:254`). An officially-dark feature can create and publish sites.
  2. **NxCloud instances are unmanageable from nav** — nxcloud route is orphaned from the sidebar *and* nxcloud-backed servers are filtered out of the Servers list (`servers/page.tsx:17`), so any provisioned nxcloud instance has no in-nav management surface.
- **P2 (notable gaps/inconsistencies):** `ENABLE_REAL_PUBLISH` stale comment (safety that doesn't exist); nxcloud order CTAs live while ordering is disabled; servers-detail tab deep-link fallback + always-on ControlPanel tab; hosting/volumes empty states delegated (verify); backup-restore "support handles it" copy contradicts self-service `BackupRestore`; deploy hub's email product discoverability.
- **P3 (polish):** duplicated `GAME_META` in deploy+games; missing "← All servers" back-link on server detail (hosting detail has one); STOPPED-server hint on volumes attach; unnecessary `force-dynamic` on the order redirect; games "Manage →" jumps into the Servers section.

The four Compute-nav list pages (servers, hosting, games, volumes), the two detail pages, and the deploy hub are coherent and current. The two genuine problems are the **orphaned/ungated surfaces**: nxcloud (off-nav, order-disabled, instances unmanageable) and sites (flag-off but route/action-open).
